title: Cliff's accompanying work and 52nd Street in 1937
summary: He accompanied early blues singers; on 52nd Street in 1937 he did not remember her.

bands.name: Cliff Jackson and His Krazy Kats

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Cliff didn't make too many records or albums, I think that there is a 78 with Cliff Jackson, an early recording in the '20s with a group, Cliff Jackson and His Krazy Kats or something like that, earlier than these selections here.

Of course, Cliff told me that he accompanied quite a few of the early blues singers. In fact on Rosetta Reitz's album, 'Mean Mothers' there is a selection in there by one of the singers in which Cliff was the accompanist. But later he just played around as a solo pianist in the local clubs.

Cliff was on 52nd Street when I came to New York in 1937 but I didn't know Cliff very well, although I had met him earlier in Pittsburgh, he happened to be sitting in the Chick Webb band and they were on a tour and I met him in 1932; and a funny thing about it, when I came to New York in 1937 I ran into Cliff on 52nd Street and I went up to him,

you know, thinking he should remember me and he ignored me like I never existed. So I said, one of these days I'm going to get even with this guy. So I followed Cliff's career and I guess we were sort of running parallel careers although he came much earlier than I did and I finally got a chance to go into Cafe Society in 1950 where he had been playing for about nine years.
